title: Writing: An Analytical Essay on Language and Communication

writingModel.placeholder: Introduce the issue using formal framing phrases
writingModel.hint: "In terms of…", "In the context of…", "With regard to…"

writingModel.placeholder: First argument — use "from the perspective of" or "in view of"
writingModel.hint: "From the perspective of ELF research…" / "In view of the evidence…"
"To the extent that X is true, Y remains the case." / "Insofar as this criticism is valid…"

writingModel.placeholder: Analysis — formal discourse phrases for nuance
writingModel.hint: "By virtue of… / In the interests of… / With a view to…"
"In light of the above…" / "As far as X is concerned, it follows that…"

writingTemplate.prefix: In the context of globalisation, the question of
writingTemplate.placeholder: which language norms should govern international communication
writingTemplate.hint: "In the context of" = formal framing phrase

writingTemplate.prefix: From the perspective of ELF research,
writingTemplate.placeholder: intelligibility and communicative effectiveness are the most appropriate benchmarks
writingTemplate.hint: "From the perspective of X" = as seen through a specific analytical lens

writingTemplate.prefix: In view of this, it follows that
writingTemplate.placeholder: the native speaker model is no longer fit for purpose in a globalised world
writingTemplate.hint: "In view of" = given this evidence, considering this

writingTemplate.prefix: To the extent that the objection has force,
writingTemplate.placeholder: it is best addressed by rethinking what "communicative success" means in international contexts
writingTemplate.hint: "To the extent that X" = qualifying the concession

writingTemplate.prefix: In light of the above, it is argued that
writingTemplate.placeholder: language education should prioritise communicative effectiveness and intercultural competence over native-speaker accuracy
writingTemplate.hint: "In light of the above" = formal conclusion phrase

items: In the context of global communication, this question has become pressing.
With regard to language policy, the evidence points clearly in one direction.
In terms of communicative effectiveness, the native speaker model is inadequate.
In relation to intercultural competence, perspective-taking is paramount.
As far as language learners are concerned, the goal should be intelligibility.
From the perspective of ELF research, intelligibility outweighs accent.
In view of the evidence, the curriculum requires fundamental revision.
By virtue of their multilingual background, these speakers have a clear advantage.
In light of recent research, the native speaker model needs rethinking.
Insofar as the model accounts for context, it remains useful.
With a view to developing intercultural competence, the curriculum was redesigned.
In the interests of equity, all language varieties deserve recognition.
For the purposes of this analysis, ELF is defined as English between non-native speakers.
With a view to improving intelligibility, the programme focuses on key features.
In the interests of learners, teachers must prioritise communicative effectiveness.
To the extent that the objection is valid, it can be addressed by redefining success.
Insofar as the model captures real differences, it remains analytically useful.
In light of the above, it follows that language education must evolve.
In view of these considerations, a pluralistic approach is recommended.
As far as global communication is concerned, flexibility matters more than accuracy.

questions.text: "___ the context of globalisation, the question of English norms has become pressing." (formal framing)
questions.hint: "In the context of" = within the domain/situation of

questions.text: "___ ___ ___ ELF research, intelligibility is the most appropriate benchmark." (from the perspective of)
questions.hint: "From the perspective of + noun" = as seen through a specific lens

questions.text: "___ ___ this evidence, the native speaker model requires revision." (given this)
"___ ___ ___ developing intercultural citizens, the curriculum was redesigned." (with the aim of)
questions.hint: "With a view to + gerund" = with the aim of

questions.text: "The objection is valid ___ ___ ___ it challenges an overly simplified model." (to the degree that)
questions.hint: "To the extent that + clause" = to the degree that

questions.text: "In the interests to equity" is grammatically correct.
"___ ___ the above discussion, it follows that communicative effectiveness should be the primary goal." (given)
questions.correct: In light of / In view of
questions.hint: "In light of / In view of + noun" = given, taking into account

questions.text: "___ ___ their diverse backgrounds, these speakers navigate intercultural communication more effectively." (because of)
questions.hint: "By virtue of + noun" = because of / on account of
